Discover how our powerful scraping platform can transform the way you extract data. Whether you're scraping e-commerce product data, collecting job listings, gathering customer reviews for sentiment analysis, or extracting any website content, our AI scrapers and workflows are designed to automate and simplify the process, giving you a powerful edge in any project. Start Here New to MrScraper? These pages get you from sign-up to your first scraped dataset. Quickstart Run your first scraper in a few minutes with a step-by-step walkthrough. Web Search Run a search query and get ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. Scraper API Test API requests, explore features, and generate code without writing code. Token Plan Learn how tokens work and create an API token for authentication. CLI Retrieve pages, search the web, and check usage from your terminal. MCP Server Connect AI clients to MrScraper for page retrieval, web search, and usage. Billing Understand subscription plans, token usage, and billing cycles. Features Explore MrScraper's key features and tools designed to make data extraction effortless. Workflow Build and customize your own scraper workflow step by step for full control. Self-Healing Let AI generate, repair, and extend workflows when a site changes. Workflow API Access Activate a scraper as an API endpoint and run it programmatically. Bulk Scraping Scrape multiple URLs in one go by uploading a list or Excel file. Proxy Route individual scrapers through proxies to mask your IP and improve reliability. Marketplace Use ready-to-run scrapers for popular websites and common scraping use cases. Scheduling Automate scraper runs on a schedule to keep your data fresh and up to date. S3 Storage Save scraped data straight into your own S3 bucket. Scraping Tips Choose the right loading path, geo-targeting, retry, and timeout settings. Cookie Use your own cookies to access content behind logins and restrictions. Team Create a team to share scrapers and collaborate on projects. Use Cases Discover how MrScraper can support different real-world scenarios. E-Commerce Scrape product details, pricing, and availability from major e-commerce sites. Job Listings Collect job postings and company data for recruitment or market analysis. Sentiment Analysis Extract and analyze customer feedback to gain insights into sentiment and satisfaction. Real Estate Gather property listings, prices, and market trends from real estate websites. Flight Price Scrape flight prices, airlines, and schedules for price monitoring and booking analysis. Optimizing Cost Minimize token usage and maximize scraping efficiency without losing accuracy. Scrape Programmatically Create an AI scraper once, then run it from your own code via the API. Integrations Integrate MrScraper with your favorite tools to automate your data flow. Email Receive email notifications whenever a scraper finishes or encounters an error. Database Automatically store scraped data in your database for querying and analysis. Webhook Send scraper results directly to external services through webhooks. Zapier Fetch pages, search the web, and check usage from no-code Zapier automations. n8n Build automated workflows around your scrapers with the MrScraper n8n node. Dify Fetch web pages and search Google from Dify agents, chatflows, and workflows. Scalekit Give AI agents per-user web fetching and search through Scalekit AgentKit. Apify Run MrScraper as Apify Actors and pipe results into the Apify platform. ClawHub Install the MrScraper skill to give your OpenClaw agent reliable web scraping. Developer Tools Work with MrScraper from your terminal, your codebase, or your AI agent. The MrScraper MCP server source code is available on GitHub for local setup, contributions, and issue reports. CLI Scrape pages, extract brand details and JSON, search the web, and check account status from your terminal. MCP Server Let AI agents fetch pages and search Google through the Model Context Protocol. Node.js SDK Scrape pages, extract brand details and JSON, search the web, and check account status with the @mrscraper/sdk package. LangChain SDK Use MrScraper as LangChain tools inside your own agents. API Reference Explore every endpoint, authentication, pagination, and error handling. Authentication Configure username patterns, sessions, and country targeting. Code Examples Ready-to-use snippets for Python, Node.js, Go, PHP, Playwright, and more. This guide shows you how to make your first scraping request with MrScraper. Make Your First API Request Before You Start Create a MrScraper account and obtain your API key from the Scraper API before following this guide. In this quickstart, you'll scrape a Walmart product page using the General AI Agent to get the following data: Product name Price Rating Number of reviews Product link cURL curl --location --request POST 'https://api.mrscraper.com?html=true' \ -H 'x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "url": "https://www.walmart.com/ip/IdeaPad-Slim-3x-15-Laptop-Snapdragon-X-X1-26-100-16GB-RAM-512GB-SSD-Luna-Grey/19075520026", "prompt": "Extract the following information in JSON format:

product_name
price
rating
number_of_reviews
product_link", "agent": "general" }' Try it in the Scraper API Run this request instantly without writing any code. The response contains the extracted data from the page. JSON { "success" : true , "data" : { "product_name" : "Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x 15.3 " Laptop AI Snapdragon X 16GB 512GB SSD Luna Grey" , "price" : 449 , "rating" : 4.5 , "number_of_reviews" : 103 , "product_link" : "https://www.walmart.com/ip/IdeaPad-Slim-3x-15-Laptop-Snapdragon-X-X1-26-100-16GB-RAM-512GB-SSD-Luna-Grey/19075520026" }, "thread_id" : "cebfaa37-f6de-45e7-8dd4-ec955824d81b" , "token_usage" : 16 , "markdown" : "" , "screenshot" : "" , "status" : "Converting data to JSON" , "error" : "" , "runtime" : 14852 } Use a Predefined Marketplace API MrScraper also provides ready-to-use scraping APIs through the Marketplace . These APIs are designed for specific industries and websites. You do not need to create prompts or extraction logic yourself. Available categories include: E-commerce News Real Estate Travel And more Explore Marketplace APIs Browse and test ready-to-use scrapers. pages.text: Scraper API | MrScraper Documentation Documentation Core Features Dashboard Getting Started Overview Quickstart Web Search Scraper API Scrape HTML Scrape Markdown Get Screenshot Scrape Brand Scrape JSON Token Plan CLI MCP Server Billing Features Workflow Workflow API Access Bulk Scraping Proxy Marketplace Schedule S3 Storage Scraping Tips Cookie Team Guides Common Use Case Optimizing Cost Create and Run a Scraper Programmatically Bulk Scraping With Custom Scraper Integrations Email SQL/Database Webhook Zapier ClawHub x402 n8n Dify Scalekit SDKs MrScraper Search ⌘ K Dashboard Documentation API Reference Residential Proxy Changelog Scraper API Scraper API Build, test, and validate scraping requests in MrScraper's Scraper API, preview results, and generate production-ready API code without coding. The Scraper API lets you build, test, and validate scraping requests without writing any code. It provides an interactive interface for configuring requests, previewing results, and generating production-ready API code. What You Can Do Test Requests Send API requests and view results instantly. Adjust Parameters Experiment with extraction settings and options. Generate Code Generate ready-to-use code snippets in multiple languages. Preview Responses Inspect the returned data before building your integration. Scraper API Overview The Scraper API has these main panels: Target URL : Configure and run the request. Example Code : Copy generated request code. Extracted Data : View the response. Settings : Adjust optional loading, rendering, and extraction options (Basic Settings, Use Cache, and Advanced Settings, plus Data Extraction in Scrape JSON). Alert Settings : Get notified when a scrape returns errors or incomplete data. Target URL In the Target URL panel, you configure and run the request: Enter the target URL. Select Run to send the request, or Reset to clear the current configuration. Select a country to load the page from. (Default to United States ) Example Code The Example Code panel builds an API request from your current configuration and updates it automatically as you make changes. Copy the code and use it directly in your application. Supported languages: cURL Python JavaScript PHP Go Java Ruby C# Agent Integration You can view the ready-made prompt for your AI coding agent to integrate MrScraper. Extracted Data The Extracted Data panel displays the response MrScraper returns after a request completes : HTTP status code Total runtime Token used Depending on the use case, the response may include: Raw HTML Markdown JSON Use this panel to confirm the extracted content matches your requirements before you integrate the request into your application. Info This panel can also show history of your previous requests and analytic of your requests. Default Parameters Parameter Description geoCode Country to load the page from, as a two-letter code. (Default to us , United States) timeout=300 Maximum seconds to wait before the request times out. Set it in Advanced Settings . Authenticate with the x-api-token header. The generated code does not repeat the token as a query parameter. Settings The settings panels contain optional features that control how MrScraper loads, renders, and extracts content. Most websites work with the default settings. Enable these options only when a website needs extra handling, such as JavaScript rendering, geographic targeting, or user interactions. Note These settings are optional. In most cases, the default configuration is enough. The available settings vary depending on the selected use case. Basic Settings Setting Description Common Use Case Default Retry Enable retry-related settings for the request. Unreliable pages or requests that fail intermittently. Off Max retries Maximum number of retries for the request. Leave empty for no limit. Limiting how many times a scrape retries. 3 Token cap Maximum total tokens the scrape and its retries can use. Controlling token usage during testing. See Token Cap . No Limit Screenshot Also captures a screenshot of the rendered page. Turning it on sends screenshot=true with browserRendering=true . Available in Scrape HTML and Scrape JSON. Confirm the page loaded correctly. Off Screenshot area Top or Full . Top captures the visible viewport at the top of the page. Full captures the entire scroll height. Available in Get Screenshot. Get the website view Full Token Cap The Token Cap limits how many tokens a single scrape and its retries can use in the Scraper API. It is available under Retry in every use case, and in Workflow. Use the token cap to keep your costs predictable. Automatic retries are bounded by the cap, so the total tokens for a single run stay at or below the value you set. This makes it easier to estimate and budget token usage while testing. For how the cap works with retries and how tokens are counted, see Scraper API Token Cap in Token Plan. Advanced Settings Advanced Settings vary by use case ; check each use case page for the full list. These settings are shared by several use cases: Setting Description Parameter Default Render JavaScript None leaves it to the API: the page loads without a browser first and switches to a browser automatically if the request is blocked. True always renders the page in a real browser, which JavaScript-heavy sites and SPAs need. False never uses a browser. browserRendering (left out for None ) None Wait for selector or text Waits until a specific CSS selector or text appears on the page before returning it. Useful for content that loads asynchronously after the initial page load. waitForSelector None Warm Start Opens the site's home page first to warm the session before loading the target URL. warmStart Off Block resources Blocks images, fonts, and stylesheets from loading. Speeds up scraping and reduces bandwidth usage. blockResources Off Timeout (s) Maximum seconds to wait for the page to fully load before the request times out. Increase for slow or complex pages. Available in every use case. timeout 300 Alert Settings The Alert Settings panel notifies you when a scrape returns errors or incomplete data. Configure where alerts go, what triggers them, and how often they're sent. Channel Choose where MrScraper sends alerts. Set one or both. Field Description Email Sends alerts to this email address. Slack Webhook URL Sends alerts to a Slack channel using an incoming webhook URL. Flag Set the conditions that trigger an alert. Type a value and press Enter to add it. Field Description Examples Error Flags Triggers an alert when the response contains one of these errors. captcha , security , 404 , 500 Data Incomplete Flags Triggers an alert when the extracted data is missing one of these fields. title , price , url Notification Rate The Identifier sets the key MrScraper uses to group alerts, so the same alert isn't sent repeatedly. Rate Limit and TTL apply separately to each group. Field Description Identifier The key used to group alerts: Domain or URL . Each group is rate-limited on its own. Rate Limit Maximum number of alerts sent per group within the TTL period. TTL (seconds) Time to Live — the length of the rate-limit period, in seconds (for example, 3600 = 1 hour). Example With a rate limit of 3 and errors on example.com and shopee.com : Domain : Grouped by domain. Once example.com hits the limit, its alerts pause for the TTL period, while shopee.com keeps its own separate count. URL : Grouped by full URL. example.com/path1 and example.com/path2 are tracked separately, so each can send its own alert. Use Cases Scrape HTML Fetch complete DOM markup with automatic proxy rotation and geo-targeting. Scrape Markdown Convert web pages into clean, LLM-friendly Markdown by stripping HTML noise and boilerplate. Get Screenshot Capture full-page or viewport screenshots of dynamic, JavaScript-rendered web pages. Scrape Brand Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and metadata as brand JSON, with optional page bundles. Scrape JSON Extract structured, strongly-typed JSON data from single pages using natural language prompts or JSON schemas. Troubleshooting If a scrape returns unexpected results, start by enabling Screenshot in the Target URL panel and inspecting the returned image. You can also copy the raw HTML and open it in an HTML viewer to see what MrScraper received. The accordion items below walk through the most common issues in the order you should check them. The page returns blank or unstyled HTML The request fails or returns an error page Web Search Run a search query with MrScraper Web Search and get ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources, without scraping the results page yourself. MrScraper uses a token-based system for both usage and authentication. Plan Tokens measure how much you can use MrScraper's features, such as running or rerunning scrapers. API Tokens allow you to securely access the MrScraper API, for example, to rerun an existing scraper programmatically. Why Token Usage Varies Token consumption isn't fixed — a few key factors affect how many tokens any given scraper uses: Website Complexity : Heavy JavaScript, dynamic content, or multiple requests increase runtime and token usage. Page Size and Content Density : Larger pages with long articles or extensive metadata produce more input text for AI models to process. Data Volume : Extracting large datasets (e.g., paginated listings) requires more compute and bandwidth. AI Processing Load : Complex instructions or large expected outputs increase input and output token usage. Keep these in mind as you read the pricing tables below — they explain why two runs on the same plan can consume different amounts of tokens. Understanding Plan Tokens Each MrScraper billing plan includes a specific number of tokens . Tokens represent the compute resources your scraper consumes — similar to how minutes or data are counted in a phone plan. The number of tokens used depends on the type of scraper you run. AI Scraper Token Usage AI Scrapers consume more tokens due to AI processing and additional factors such as: Usage Type Description Conversion Rate Run Tracking Each AI agent run consumes 5 tokens for trace tracking. Reruns and workflows consume 0 tokens for this component. 0 or 5 tokens per run Runtime Time spent processing your task. 1 token per 30 seconds of runtime Input Tokens Amount of text data (prompts or instructions) sent to the AI model. 1 token per ~1,000 input tokens Output Tokens Amount of text generated by the AI model (responses or extracted results). 1 token per ~200 output tokens Example If your AI scraper runs for 90 seconds , processes 5,000 input tokens , and generates 1,000 output tokens , your total token usage would be: Component Calculation Tokens Runtime 90 ÷ 30 3 Input 5,000 ÷ 1,000 5 Output 1,000 ÷ 200 5 Run Trace Fixed 5 Total 18 Note Each run automatically includes trace tracking for debugging and performance monitoring. Input and output tokens are based on how much text the AI model processes and generates. AI Scrapers tend to consume more tokens due to model processing. Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1). Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage Workflows and Scrape HTML consume tokens based on two factors: runtime and bandwidth . Usage Type Description Conversion Rate Runtime Time your scraper runs. 1 token per 30 seconds Bandwidth Amount of data downloaded or uploaded. 1 token per 0.25 MB Example If your workflow or Scrape HTML request runs for 40 seconds and uses 1.1 MB of bandwidth: Component Calculation Tokens Runtime 40 ÷ 30 = 1.33 → rounded up 2 Bandwidth 1.1 ÷ 0.25 = 4.4 → rounded up 5 Total 7 Note Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1). Scraper API Token Cap The Scraper API token cap limits how many tokens a single scrape can use in the Scraper API. It is available in Workflow and under Retry in every Scraper API use case. For Workflow and Scrape HTML, tokens are counted with the runtime and bandwidth calculations shown in Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage . When Retry is enabled, a failed scrape retries automatically. Two limits control how far retrying goes: Max retries : The maximum number of retry attempts (3 by default). Token cap : The maximum total tokens all attempts can use (Unlimited by default). Retrying stops at the first of these: the scrape succeeds, it reaches Max retries, or the running token total reaches the token cap. Each attempt's token cost is rounded up (ceiling rule) and added to a running total. The token cap takes effect only when Retry is enabled, since its purpose is to limit how many tokens retries can consume. If Retry is off, the scrape runs once and returns a result or an error. Example The scrape succeeds Stops at Max retries Stops at the Token Cap Max retries 3 , token cap 10 . Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 2.4 tokens 3 3 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 1.6 tokens 2 5 Succeeded The scrape succeeds on the second attempt, using 5 tokens. Because it succeeded, the Scraper API returns the result and stops even though max retries and tokens still remain (5 of 10 tokens left, and 2 retries unused). Max retries 2 , token cap 20 . Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 3.6 tokens 4 4 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 3.8 tokens 4 8 Failed, retrying 3 (retry 2) 3.4 tokens 4 12 Failed, max retries reached The scrape uses both retries without succeeding, so it stops even though 8 tokens still remain under the 20-token cap. Max retries 3 , token cap 12 , about 4 tokens per run. Attempt Runtime + Bandwidth Rounded-up Cost Running Total Result 1 (initial) 3.5 tokens 4 4 Failed, retrying 2 (retry 1) 3.9 tokens 4 8 Failed, retrying 3 (retry 2) 3.7 tokens 4 12 Failed, cap reached The running total reaches the 12-token cap on the second retry, so the scrape stops before using all 3 retries. First attempt exceeds the cap If the first attempt costs more than the cap (for example, a cap of 10 but a first scrape that needs 15 tokens), the scrape still runs once but doesn't retry. It returns either a result or an error. Set the token cap high enough to allow for retries, especially on pages with variable load times or bandwidth. If a scrape hits the cap before completing, try increasing the cap. Marketplace Scraper Token Usage Marketplace Scrapers use a custom token cost based on factors such as the target domain, workflow complexity, proxy usage, infrastructure requirements, and scraper configuration. Each scraper may use either a fixed token cost or a custom usage calculation depending on how the scraper is designed. For the complete list of Marketplace Scraper token costs, see the Marketplace catalog. The MrScraper CLI provides terminal access to the seven MrScraper services, with browser sign-in and optional agent skill setup. Its commands share their descriptions, parameter meanings, and defaults with the MCP server , the SDKs, and the other integrations. This guide covers installation, authentication, output, environment variables, programmatic usage, and complete command details. Command Description status Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. scrape-html Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. scrape-markdown Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. get-screenshot Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. scrape-brand Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. scrape-json Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. web-search Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. init , login , auth status , logout , and setup skills are configuration commands. Requirements Node.js 20 or newer A MrScraper account for browser login, or an API key for non-interactive use Package information This page documents version 0.7.1 . Version 0.7.0 replaced scraperAPI with scrape-html , scrape-markdown , and get-screenshot , replaced account with status , added scrape-brand and scrape-json , renamed webSearch to web-search , and switched to a three-skill pack. See Migrating from 0.6.x . See @mrscraper/cli on npm for the current published version. Installation Install only the CLI globally: npm install -g @mrscraper/cli@latest mrscraper --version Install the CLI and the MrScraper agent skill pack for every detected harness: npx -y @mrscraper/cli@latest init --all Install for one harness: npx -y @mrscraper/cli@latest init --agent codex Supported IDs are claude-code , cursor , codex , grok , hermes , opencode , openclaw , pi , and omp . The skill pack contains three skills: mrscraper for setup and account usage, mrscraper-fetch for page retrieval, and mrscraper-serp for web search. Copyable AI setup prompt Read and follow https://github.com/mrscraper-com/cli/blob/main/skills/mrscraper/SKILL.md For an agent-controlled, non-interactive setup, skip authentication during bootstrap and start login separately: npx -y @mrscraper/cli@latest init --agent codex --yes --skip-auth mrscraper auth status --json mrscraper login CLI and skills only mrscraper init installs the CLI and skill pack. It does not install or configure MCP. It accepts --agent <id> for one harness and --dry-run ; without --agent , it targets detected harnesses. mrscraper setup skills mrscraper setup skills --agent hermes mrscraper init --all --yes --skip-auth --dry-run Native plugins (optional) Native agent plugins are maintained separately from the CLI for ChatGPT and Codex and Claude . Verifying installation After completing installation, verify that the CLI binary and commands are accessible in your environment: mrscraper --version mrscraper auth status --json mrscraper status A successful status call confirms that the CLI can load its authentication and reach the MrScraper service. Skill pack reloading Restart an agent harness or open a new terminal session after installing skills so it reloads the skill pack properly. Authentication Browser login mrscraper login The CLI opens the MrScraper login page, waits for browser approval, and saves a dedicated API key in ~/.mrscraper/auth.json . Keep mrscraper login running until approval completes. Set MRSCRAPER_HOME to change the containing directory. API-key login mrscraper login --api-key " $MRSCRAPER_API_KEY " For automation, set an environment variable instead of saving a key: export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY = "YOUR_TOKEN" Authentication precedence for service commands is: Command --token MRSCRAPER_API_KEY MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN ~/.mrscraper/auth.json --token is sent in request headers, never in the request URL. login parameters Parameter Default Scope Behavior --api-key <key> — Local Saves this API key and does not open browser login. --token <key> — Local Deprecated alias for login's --api-key . --no-browser off Local Prompts a human for an API key; requires an interactive terminal. --no-open off Local Prints the browser sign-in URL without launching it. The CLI still waits for approval. --timeout <seconds> 180 Local Maximum time to wait for browser approval. Auth status and logout mrscraper auth status reports the credential currently available to the CLI. It reads the local configuration without sending a test request. JSON output uses the credential_configured field, plus source for an environment variable or path for a saved key: { "credential_configured" : true , "auth_type" : "api_key" , "path" : "/home/user/.mrscraper/auth.json" } mrscraper logout deletes local credential files. It does not revoke an API key remotely. Output Every service command prints a JSON envelope to stdout: { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>" , "headers" : { "content-type" : "text/html; charset=utf-8" } } status_code contains the HTTP response code. data contains the API response body. JSON bodies are parsed; other bodies, such as HTML or Markdown text, remain strings. Field names are returned as the API sends them. headers contains response headers. Credential-bearing headers are filtered, and known credential metadata in scraping and search JSON is redacted. status preserves its body fields. Failed API calls print a JSON envelope with error and exit non-zero. HTTP failures keep the status in status_code ; network failures use null . Progress messages use stderr so stdout stays machine-readable. Invalid arguments fail before any request. Save large output with shell redirection: mrscraper scrape-html https://example.com > result.json mrscraper scrape-markdown https://example.com | jq -r '.data' Response examples on this page show selected keys with placeholder values. Actual responses may contain additional fields. Environment variables Variable Default Purpose MRSCRAPER_API_KEY — Preferred API-key environment override. MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN — Alternative API-key environment override. MRSCRAPER_HOME ~/.mrscraper Credential directory override. MRSCRAPER_API_BASE_URL https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1 Development override for status and login. MRSCRAPER_FETCH_BASE_URL https://api.mrscraper.com Development override for scraping and search commands. The CLI also loads a .env file from the current working directory. Shared parameters Service options use kebab-case. Run mrscraper <command> --help to see the options a command accepts. Every service command also accepts --token <key> . Page controls scrape-html , scrape-markdown , get-screenshot , and scrape-json accept these options. Page defaults are 300 seconds, US geolocation and proxy country, real-device routing off, and dashboard saving off. Omitted retry limits mean no limit. Parameter API field Type Default Description <url> url string Required Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. --timeout timeout integer 300 Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. --geo-code geoCode string "us" Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. --proxy-country proxyCountry string "us" Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. --super super boolean false Whether to route the request through real devices. --wait-until waitUntil string: domcontentloaded , load , networkidle0 , networkidle2 "domcontentloaded" Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. --proxy proxy string Omitted Custom proxy URL used to load the page. --max-retries maxRetries integer Omitted Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. --save-result saveResult boolean false Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. Loading controls scrape-html , scrape-markdown , and get-screenshot also accept these options. scrape-json does not. Parameter API field Type Default Description --block-resources blockResources boolean false Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. --wait-for-selector waitForSelector string Omitted Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. --return-cookie returnCookie boolean false Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. Browser rendering is optional for HTML, Markdown, and JSON; screenshots always enable it. Markdown with HTML also enables browser rendering. CLI command list status Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. It takes no service parameters, and its HTTP deadline is fixed at 600 seconds. --json is accepted for compatibility; JSON is already the default. mrscraper status mrscraper status | jq '.data.data.tokenUsage' The API body contains message and data . Account details remain nested in data , including subscriptionItem and scraperAllowance , so the envelope exposes them at data.data . { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "message" : "Example response" , "data" : { "id" : "ACCOUNT_ID" , "tokenLimit" : 100000 , "tokenUsage" : 2500 , "stripeStatus" : "active" , "user" : { "name" : "Example user" , "email" : "user@example.com" , "isVerified" : true }, "subscriptionItem" : { "name" : "Example plan" , "tokenLimit" : 100000 }, "scraperAllowance" : { "remaining" : 97500 , "plans" : [{ "remaining" : 97500 }] } } }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } scrape-html Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. Accepts page controls , loading controls , and: Parameter API field Type Default Description --browser-rendering browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. --warm-start warmStart boolean false Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. mrscraper scrape-html https://example.com --browser-rendering --warm-start \ --wait-for-selector 'body' --timeout 120 --max-retries 0 The default response body is HTML text. Additional controls can cause the API to return JSON; the returned structure is preserved. Scrape HTML usage is based on runtime and bandwidth. Resource blocking can reduce bandwidth for text-focused pages, and --max-retries limits retry usage. See the Token Plan for the complete calculation. scrape-markdown Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. Accepts page controls , loading controls , and: Parameter API field Type Default Description --browser-rendering browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. --warm-start warmStart boolean false Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. --html html boolean false Whether to include the page HTML in the response. mrscraper scrape-markdown https://example.com --html --warm-start The default response body is Markdown text. With --html , data is an object containing both outputs: { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "html" : "<html>...</html>" , "markdown" : "# Example page 

 ..." }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } get-screenshot Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. Accepts page controls , loading controls , and: Parameter API field Type Default Description --screenshot screenshot string: full , top "full" Screenshot area to capture: full for the entire page or top for the top viewport. --no-html html boolean true Sets html=false . Whether to include the page HTML in the response. --markdown markdown boolean false Whether to include the page Markdown in the response. mrscraper get-screenshot https://example.com --screenshot top --no-html --markdown mrscraper get-screenshot https://example.com --no-html | jq -r '.data.screenshot' | base64 -d > page.png The response body contains a base64 screenshot and the requested page outputs. The API can still include HTML when HTML output is disabled. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "html" : "<html>...</html>" , "screenshot" : "BASE64_PNG_DATA" , "markdown" : "# Example page 

 ..." }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } scrape-brand Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. It takes only the URL; page controls are not accepted. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. mrscraper scrape-brand https://example.com The API body contains message and a data object with job_id , status , url , final_url , brand , and error . Brand details are at data.data.brand . { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "data" : { "job_id" : "JOB_ID" , "status" : "succeeded" , "url" : "https://example.com" , "final_url" : "https://example.com" , "brand" : { "name" : "Example brand" , "colors" : { "background" : "#ffffff" , "text" : "#222222" }, "typography" : { "body" : { "font_family" : "Example font" } } }, "error" : null , "bundle_url" : null }, "message" : "Example response" }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } scrape-json Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. Accepts page controls and: Parameter API field Type Default Description --prompt prompt string "Extract all data as complete as possible." Instructions describing the data to extract. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. --browser-rendering browserRendering boolean false Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. --html html boolean false Whether to include the page HTML in the response. --screenshot screenshot boolean false Whether to include a base64 screenshot in the response. mrscraper scrape-json https://example.com --browser-rendering \ --prompt 'Extract the first 2 items with title and price. Json Schema: {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"price":{"type":"string"}},"required":["title","price"]}}' Extraction results are in the API body's data field and follow the requested schema. Response metadata includes thread_id , token_usage , status , error , runtime , and cookies . html , markdown , and screenshot can be empty strings when not requested. { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "success" : true , "data" : [{ "title" : "Example item" , "price" : "10.00" }], "thread_id" : "THREAD_ID" , "token_usage" : 1 , "html" : "" , "markdown" : "" , "screenshot" : "" , "status" : "Results ready" , "error" : "" , "runtime" : 1.23 , "cookies" : [] }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json" } } web-search Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. Parameter API field Type Default Description <query> query string Required Search query text, trimmed before sending, containing 1 to 1000 characters. --country country string "us" Two-letter country code to search from, sent in lowercase. --num-results numResults integer 10 Number of search results to request, as an integer from 10 to 100. Fewer results may be returned. mrscraper web-search "site:example.com documentation" --country id --num-results 20 The API body contains success , message , a data array, and tokenUsage . Each result includes rank , title , url , description , and source . { "status_code" : 200 , "data" : { "success" : true , "message" : "Example response" , "data" : [ { "rank" : 1 , "title" : "Example result" , "url" : "https://example.com" , "description" : "Example result description." , "source" : "example.com" } ], "tokenUsage" : 1 }, "headers" : { "content-type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" } } Programmatic use The package exports the low-level functions used by the commands: scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , getScreenshot , scrapeBrand , scrapeJson , webSearch , and getSubscriptionAccountApi . import { scrapeMarkdown, webSearch, getSubscriptionAccountApi } from "@mrscraper/cli" ; const token = process.env. MRSCRAPER_API_KEY ; const page = await scrapeMarkdown ({ token, url: "https://example.com" }); console. log (page.data); const results = await webSearch ({ token, query: "books" , country: "us" , numResults: 10 }); for ( const item of results.data.data) console. log (item.rank, item.title, item.url); const status = await getSubscriptionAccountApi (token); console. log (status.data.data.tokenUsage); The functions take a single options object and return the same envelope the commands print. Options use camelCase, and the JavaScript option for super is superMode . getSubscriptionAccountApi takes the token as its only argument. Programmatic calls require an explicit token and do not load saved CLI credentials or .env files. For an application client, prefer the Node.js SDK . Troubleshooting For missing credentials, run mrscraper login or set MRSCRAPER_API_KEY . For slow pages, increase --timeout up to 300 seconds. scrape-brand and web-search have fixed 120-second deadlines. Use --help on a command to inspect its accepted options. The old command names are not kept as aliases. 0.6.x 0.7.x mrscraper scraperAPI <url> mrscraper scrape-html <url> mrscraper scraperAPI <url> --no-html --markdown mrscraper scrape-markdown <url> mrscraper scraperAPI <url> --markdown mrscraper scrape-markdown <url> --html mrscraper scraperAPI <url> --no-html --screenshot mrscraper get-screenshot <url> --no-html mrscraper scraperAPI <url> --home-page mrscraper scrape-html <url> --warm-start mrscraper webSearch <query> mrscraper web-search <query> mrscraper account mrscraper status scraperAPI({ token, url, ... }) scrapeHtml , scrapeMarkdown , or getScreenshot account({ token }) getSubscriptionAccountApi(token) status prints the raw API body as JSON. The 0.6.x summary at data.account , the terminal dashboard, and the --pretty and --no-color options are gone. status and web-search no longer accept --timeout . Defaults changed: page --timeout is now 300 , --geo-code and --proxy-country default to us , and an omitted --max-retries means no limit. --no-use-proxy , --bypass-proxy , --cookie-jar , --headers , --token-cap , --stream , --discard-token-secret , --no-browser-rendering , and --save are removed. Use shell redirection instead of --save . The skill pack changed from four skills ( mrscraper , mrscraper-scraper-api , mrscraper-account , mrscraper-web-search ) to three ( mrscraper , mrscraper-fetch , mrscraper-serp ).
